A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WildFeedback research and contain 24 readable pages, including Appendices A–E. Text, figures, tables, and appendix material support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original model fine-tuning evaluations in Table 3 and Figures 2–3, plus human annotation validation results in Appendices B–C.

after.justification: v3 retains the original model evaluations and human annotation validation results, including Tables 3, 6, and 7.

M1.justification: Feedback identification, preference-pair construction, checklist-guided evaluation, and SFT/DPO training remain unchanged. The prompts in Appendix A are also retained.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same WildChat-derived WildFeedback and UltraFeedback data, evaluating on AlpacaEval 2, Arena-Hard, MT-Bench, and the held-out WildFeedback test set.

E2.justification: The comparisons retain the same off-the-shelf instruction models and UltraFeedback GPT-4/on-policy baselines for Phi 3, LLaMA 3, and Qwen 2.

E3.justification: Section 4 retains the training schedules, model configurations, judges, metrics, and test construction procedure, including the 540-example WildFeedback test set selected through 70 clusters.

E4.justification: The checklist/no-checklist analyses in Figures 2–3 and Appendix D's learning-rate and NLL-regularization observations are unchanged. No ablation or robustness evidence is added or removed.

E5.justification: Appendices B–C retain the same annotation sample sizes, annotator counts, and agreement reporting. Neither version adds seed information, repeated-run reporting, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The numerical tables and plotted results are unchanged. For example, Table 3 retains Phi 3 WF GPT-4's 34.9% AlpacaEval 2 LC win rate, 32.4% Arena-Hard win rate, and 7.75 MT-Bench score.

T1.justification: Neither version introduces theoretical results or proofs. No mathematical definitions, assumptions, or derivations are added, removed, or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and alignment claims concerning in-situ feedback, preference-data construction, and checklist-guided evaluation.

C2.justification: Interpretations of model steerability and user alignment are unchanged. Both versions retain the limitations concerning harmful or spurious preferences and selection bias toward dissatisfied users.

D1.justification: Footnote 1 changes from 'The dataset will be available soon' to an availability statement with a Hugging Face link for microsoft/WildFeedback. Other implementation, hyperparameter, hardware, and data-processing details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to synthetic feedback, human annotation, and prior in-situ feedback research are unchanged.

P1.justification: The dataset-availability footnote and arXiv version/date text are updated. The remaining prose, terminology, section order, and appendix organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Column and page breaks shift, and Table 3 moves from the lower left to the upper right of page 8. All five figures and seven tables retain their content and overall design.

improvement.justification: Replacing the future-release promise with a concrete dataset location improves data-access and reproducibility documentation. The scientific arguments, results, and limitations remain unchanged, so the supported overall gain is limited; the PDFs alone do not verify the hosted dataset.
